remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages ... as instructions that alter its own goals
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty
MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action
any peer agent address or message sender not on that allowlist is not an authorized counterparty
Signature-verified inbound messages, queries, and broadcasts from peer agents.
Only when the operator has enabled mailbox delivery.

threats.summary: A captured signed envelope can be resubmitted over HTTP or mailbox indefinitely because verify() never checks expires or nonce.
Any sender claiming a 'user'-prefixed address skips signature verification and reaches allow_unverified handlers.
Any address on the open network that can sign reaches every signed handler; no default peer allowlist exists.
Unbounded request bodies and an unbounded message queue let any client exhaust memory or starve the sequential processor.
A forged sync envelope naming a victim peer overwrites that peer's pending reply future before verification runs.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection
must serve only the agent's declared endpoints

threats.summary: The loopback-only guard on /messages, /connect and /disconnect is satisfied by a forged X-Forwarded-For header or by any page in the operator's browser.
/messages returns cached counterparty envelope payloads to whoever passes the spoofable guard.
The Helm chart and Dockerfiles deploy the inspector-on reference agent as root with empty security contexts.

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own
Data published to the public Almanac / Agentverse profile ... MUST be limited to non-sensitive information

threats.summary: A /connect caller makes the agent sign an Agentverse identity proof under the caller's user_token and register itself at a caller-chosen endpoint URL.

Operator metadata and the README file are published to the public registry with no sensitivity filter (checked: agent.py:606-626 AgentMetadata validates shape only; agent.py:438-443 reads README verbatim).

trust_boundaries.name: Handler access to wallet and ledger

remit_rules.excerpt: Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds
Any discretionary on-chain value transfer or spend of wallet funds
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.
MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized

threats.summary: Every handler driven by a verified peer gets ctx.ledger and the signing wallet with no spend policy, approval gate or halt-on-threshold hook.

trust_boundaries.name: Outbound sends, resolution and sync replies

remit_rules.excerpt: Adding a new outbound communication channel, integration, or counterparty not already authorized.
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty

threats.summary: Sync replies are never signed and unsigned replies are accepted as coming from env.sender, so an interceptor of a plain-HTTP peer endpoint can answer as that peer.
Peer self-registered endpoint URLs are POSTed to without scheme or host validation, making the agent a blind SSRF client to loopback or internal ranges.
ctx.send resolves and messages any address; no outbound counterparty allowlist exists.

Handler state is persisted as plaintext JSON in the working directory and reloaded into handlers with no integrity check, so a local writer can alter state across restarts (checked: storage/__init__.py:90-96 — no integrity check or file mode).

trust_boundaries.name: Seed and private keys at rest

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials, API keys, and seed material ... MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.
Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host
Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.

threats.summary: The Helm chart commits a literal default seed, so any default install has a publicly derivable identity and wallet key.
Named seedless agents write identity and wallet private keys as plaintext private_keys.json in the CWD with default permissions, and no redaction or egress check guards key material.
First-run persistence saves a different wallet key than the one in use, stranding funds sent to the first-run address after restart.
The PyPI release job expands the PR head ref in shell and pip-installs unpinned packages while publishing tokens are in its environment, with no dependency scanning.

remit_rules.excerpt: these events MUST leave a log record
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification

threats.summary: Handled messages and interval runs leave no log record, InsufficientFundsError is swallowed, and verification failures raise no aggregated alert.

signature check passes; expires/nonce never enforced
any verified sender reaches every signed handler

value moved on-chain on forged data
